classification.difficultyReason: Combine angle facts at a point, parallel-line properties and triangle angle sums, giving reasons.

content.prompt: Find the angles marked with pronumerals. Give reasons for your answers.

spec.description: Straight line AC, upward ray VB, downward-right ray VD, right-angle square in BVC and the source angle labels.
spec.mathematics: A,V,C are collinear; angle BVC is 90 degrees; angle CVD is 65 degrees; alpha is AVB and beta is AVD below AC.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and unknown labels are visible.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\alpha&=180^{\circ}-90^{\circ}\\\alpha&=90^{\circ}\\\beta&=180^{\circ}-65^{\circ}\\\beta&=115^{\circ}\end{align*}$$
Both calculations use adjacent angles on a straight line.

spec.description: Two straight lines QS and RU cross at P; ray PT lies between PS and PU.
spec.mathematics: QPR=35 degrees; SPT=15 degrees; alpha=TPU; beta=RPS.

answer.worked:
Vertically opposite angles give $\angle SPU=35^{\circ}$.
$$\begin{align*}\alpha&=35^{\circ}-15^{\circ}\\\alpha&=20^{\circ}\\\beta&=180^{\circ}-35^{\circ}\\\beta&=145^{\circ}\end{align*}$$
The last calculation uses adjacent angles on the straight line QS.

spec.description: Zigzag ABCD with matching single parallel arrows on AB and CD and an exterior reflex arc at C.
spec.mathematics: AB is parallel to CD; reflex BCD=326 degrees; alpha=ABC.
spec.answerVisibility: The interior angle at C is not supplied.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\angle BCD&=360^{\circ}-326^{\circ}\\\angle BCD&=34^{\circ}\\\alpha&=34^{\circ}\end{align*}$$
Angles in a revolution total $360^{\circ}$. Then $\alpha=\angle BCD$ by alternate angles, since $AB\parallel CD$.

spec.description: Right triangle JNM with L on JM, joined triangle JKL, and the exterior reflex angle at J.
spec.mathematics: JNM=90 degrees; JMN=30 degrees; JKL=70 degrees; reflex NJK=252 degrees. Alpha=NJM, beta=MJK, theta=JLK.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the printed angles and unknown labels are shown; no extra parallel marks are added.

answer.worked:
Use the angle sum of $\triangle JNM$:
$$\begin{align*}\alpha&=180^{\circ}-90^{\circ}-30^{\circ}\\\alpha&=60^{\circ}\end{align*}$$
Use angles in a revolution at J:
$$\begin{align*}\beta&=360^{\circ}-252^{\circ}-60^{\circ}\\\beta&=48^{\circ}\end{align*}$$
Use the angle sum of $\triangle JKL$:
$$\begin{align*}\theta&=180^{\circ}-70^{\circ}-48^{\circ}\\\theta&=62^{\circ}\end{align*}$$

spec.description: A right angle MLK split by LN, with a reflex arc around the outside from LM to LK.
spec.mathematics: MLK=90 degrees; NLK=42 degrees; alpha=MLN; beta is the reflex MLK.
spec.answerVisibility: Unknown alpha and beta remain symbolic.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\alpha&=90^{\circ}-42^{\circ}\\\alpha&=48^{\circ}\\\beta&=360^{\circ}-90^{\circ}\\\beta&=270^{\circ}\end{align*}$$
The two inner angles are complementary. The right angle and reflex angle form a revolution.

spec.description: Adjacent quadrilaterals ABCF and FCDE. Distinct single and double parallel-arrow families are retained.
spec.mathematics: A,F,E are collinear; B,C,D are collinear; AB parallel CF parallel DE; BC parallel AF; FCD=120 degrees; alpha=BAF; beta=ABC.
spec.answerVisibility: No inferred angle values or quadrilateral names are printed.

answer.worked:
Since $AB\parallel FC$, corresponding angles give $\beta=\angle FCD=120^{\circ}$.
Since $AE\parallel BD$, co-interior angles give:
$$\begin{align*}\alpha&=180^{\circ}-120^{\circ}\\\alpha&=60^{\circ}\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Parallel descending lines AB and CD crossed by FKE and HMG. Only AB and CD carry parallel arrows; a right-angle square is at K.
spec.mathematics: A,J,L,B are collinear; C,K,M,D are collinear; F,K,J,E are collinear; H,M,L,G are collinear; AB parallel CD; JKM=90 degrees; BLM=87 degrees; alpha=AJK; beta=KMH. The ascending transversals are not marked parallel.
spec.answerVisibility: The student sees only the original right-angle mark, 87-degree given, parallel marks and unknown labels.

answer.worked:
Since $AB\parallel CD$, alternate angles give $\alpha=\angle JKM=90^{\circ}$ and $\angle LMK=\angle BLM=87^{\circ}$.
Angles on the straight line HML give:
$$\begin{align*}\beta&=180^{\circ}-87^{\circ}\\\beta&=93^{\circ}\end{align*}$$
